This supports local s/ś > h rather than a distant donor.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 1388.1 ālu/āluka originally names edible aroid roots; it explicitly records Hindi ālū, Punjabi ālū and Nepali ālu ‘potato’, with an addendum’s Kotgarhi aḷu ‘potato’. The modern crop meaning is a semantic transfer, not a claim that the ancient Sanskrit word named the potato; regional borrowing/reinforcement and local vowel length/gemination remain qualified, so the provisional reflex relation needs review alongside possible contact transmission.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 4715 gives Prakrit calaï, Hindi calnā and Old Marwari calaï; contrast long-vowel cāl- under 4721. Each selected pair has two inflections of this same stem (cal-re includes a vocative particle); no gayo or other auxiliary is present. The survey’s vowel lengths and eastern e-vowels may not uniquely distinguish calati from calyati, and Turner documents contact spread into eastern languages.

Its addenda derive vaḍra by extraction from formations such as evaḍa/kevaḍa, ultimately involving -vant plus -ḍa; this is not a simple direct descent from vṛddha. Regional vowel and liquid variation remains for triage.

proposals.evidence: Proposed full reduplication of alag ‘different/separate’, with CDIAL 700 alagna supporting the base family. Repetition is an analysis of the survey form, not a separately reconstructed ancient compound. The alag anchor is from Sonipura-Balai, while these repeated forms occur at other survey sites; it represents the proposed survey-level base, not evidence that one village borrowed from another. Acceptance depends on Nimadi proposal 176; local vowel length and the precise distributive nuance remain qualified.

No specific contact donor is established.
